newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Clarke interested in party's top job.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Clarke interested in party's top job.

text.p: British finance minister Kenneth Clarke suggested that he would be pitching for the top job in the Conservative Party if it loses the election and John Major stands down, a newspaper said on Wednesday.
The Daily Mail added that Clarke also expressed an interest in being prime minister.
"I find the leadership of a party that has won the election rather more attractive than the leadership of a party which has lost the election," the newspaper quoted his as saying.
With less than four months left before Major must call an election, the Conservatives are still trailing the opposition Labour Party by up to 20 points, according to the latest opinion polls.
Clarke also rebuked colleagues for privately plotting for the party leadership saying it could damage the party in the run-up to the election which must be held by May 22.

Some members of parliament have viewed the row between Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine and Defence Secretary Michael Portillo over the government's decision to pay 60 million pounds ($97 million) for a new royal yacht as sparring for the party leadership.

"Any politician who is going around governing his utterances or activities by planning whether he is going to be a leadership contender is frankly adopting a rather unhelpful approach to the job," Clarke said. ($1=.6199 Pound)
